pattern_explanation: Both languages borrowed these words from the same Latin roots, so the spellings stayed close, but their meanings drifted apart over centuries of separate use.
false_friend_warning: The Spanish word that looks like English 'sensible' actually means 'sensitive' in English, so learners who translate it literally will say 'sensible' when they mean someone is easily hurt or emotionally responsive. The same kind of trap applies to 'actual', which means 'current' rather than 'real'.
